I don't have search access outside this directory, and this working directory itself has no files in it (no packet folder or tracking tool present), so I can't inspect the actual packet contents directly — I'm going on your description.

Based on what you've told me: `add-dark-mode-toggle` is genuinely dead, not just stale. The team explicitly decided against it last month, nothing from it ever merged, and it's still just placeholder scaffolding. That's different from `refactor-auth-flow`, which is invalid-tagged but actively being worked on — that one just needs its teammate to finish adding the missing file; it shouldn't be touched.

For `add-dark-mode-toggle`, I'd delete the packet folder outright rather than leave it around:

- It has no merged work to preserve.
- "Scaffold with placeholder text" means there's no real content to archive for later reference.
- If you want a paper trail for the decision, the team meeting notes (or wherever that decision was recorded) already serve that purpose — you don't need to keep a stale folder as a substitute for that record.

If you'd rather keep a trace of it instead of deleting (e.g., in case the color-palette work resumes later and someone wants the sketch as a starting point), the alternative is to move it out of the scanned directory (e.g., into an `archive/` folder or a git branch) so the status check stops flagging it, without losing the content.

Want me to locate the actual packets directory (I'd need permission to browse outside this folder) so I can do the removal, or do you want to handle the delete/move yourself?
